body:
Local CLI providers (claude, codex, agy, agent) are resolved by bare command name via resolveCommand and then spawned by execCli. Two paths resolve by name: (1) fresh detection in configureLLM (the ladder + isCmdInstalled), and (2) cache reuse in cachedResolutionUsable. As of feat/provider-model-config, the cache-reuse path canonicalizes the resolved executable and returns false when it is inside the current working directory; fresh detection does not perform that containment check.

npm and npx prepend ./node_modules/.bin to PATH. A repository can therefore expose a bin named claude/codex/agy that fresh detection selects and execCli spawns with the invoking process's privileges and environment.

Reproduction: in a repository that has node_modules/.bin/codex present, with no API credentials set, run the tool (e.g. via an npm script). Auto-detection selects codex and execCli spawns the repository-local binary.

Change: introduce a single CLI resolver used by fresh detection, cache reuse, and spawn. It canonicalizes the executable path (resolving symlinks), returns null/refuses when the resolved path is contained within the working-tree root, and returns the validated absolute path. Spawn that exact validated path rather than re-resolving the bare name at execCli time.

Acceptance criteria:
- AC1: with a repo-local node_modules/.bin/<cli> present and no API keys, detection does not select or spawn the repo-local binary (it either selects a CLI resolved outside the tree or reports no provider).
- AC2: a globally installed CLI whose path is outside the working tree is still selected and spawned.
- AC3: fresh detection and cache reuse call the same resolver; the spawn uses the validated absolute path.
- AC4: integration test with a fabricated repo-local CLI on PATH proves AC1; full suite green.

Related: T21 (persist-after-success), T23 (config path containment). Some CLI-harness test files are declared as T7 rails; coordinate edits accordingly.
title: Reject repository-local CLI executables in both fresh detection and cache reuse (single shared resolver)
